Make a PHW-styled reactable

Source: R/html-widgets.R
phw_reactable.Rd

Calls reactable::reactable() with the PHW theme, striping, compact rows and number formatting with thousands separators. It also attaches the Ubuntu web font. You can add a title above and a source line below.

Usage

phw_reactable(
  data,
  ...,
  caption = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  header = "booktabs",
  accent = phw_colours[["navy"]],
  caption_args = list(),
  digits = 1,
  group_col = NULL,
  key = NULL,
  palette = phw_default_palette()
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, or a summary table from phw_summary_table(), phw_crosstab(), phw_rate_table() or phw_risk_table() (shown with bold headings, indented levels and no sorting or paging).

...

Passed to reactable::reactable(). Any of them, including theme, defaultColDef and language, replace the PHW defaults.

caption

Optional title shown above the table.

source, date

Passed to phw_caption() and shown below the table.

header, accent

Passed to phw_reactable_theme().

caption_args

List of other phw_caption() arguments.

digits

Decimal places for non-integer numbers, as in phw_flextable() and phw_gt(). A column of whole numbers shows none. A column you format yourself in columns or ... keeps your format.

group_col, key, palette

Colour the cells of the column group_col (unquoted as in dplyr, or a string) by group, with the same colours as your charts. key and palette are passed to phw_colour_key().

Value

An htmlwidget (or a tag list when a caption or source is given).

Examples

if (requireNamespace("reactable", quietly = TRUE)) {
  df <- data.frame(area = paste("Area", LETTERS[1:5]),
                   group = c("Group A", "Group B", "Group A", "Group C", "Group B"),
                   cases = c(1203, 845, 642, 190, 231))
  tbl <- phw_reactable(df, caption = "Cases by area", source = "Example data",
                       searchable = TRUE)

  # Colour the group column with the same colours as your charts
  tbl2 <- phw_reactable(df, group_col = group)

  # A summary table keeps its bold headings and indents
  ll <- data.frame(sex = rep(c("Female", "Male"), 10),
                   outcome = rep(c("Outcome X", "Outcome Y"), each = 10))
  tbl3 <- phw_reactable(phw_summary_table(ll, by = outcome))

  # Printing shows the table in the Viewer or a browser.
  if (interactive()) print(tbl)
}
